chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Humran, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about a woman who married during her waiting period out of ignorance on her part regarding that. He said, then he said: 'I do not see any penalty upon her, and she is separated from the one she married, and she does not become permissible to him ever.'

I said: 'And if she had known that that was forbidden upon her, then she proceeded to do so?' He said: 'If she married him during the waiting period of her husband who divorced her with a revocable divorce (raj'ah), then I see that the penalty of stoning is upon her. And if she married during the waiting period of her husband who divorced her with a non-revocable divorce, then I see that the punishment of the fornicator is upon her, and she is separated from the one who married her, and she does not become permissible to him ever.'

key_terms.لاَ تَحِلُّ لَهُ أَبَداً: she does not become permissible to him ever

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling and penalty for a woman who marries during her waiting period after divorce?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) distinguishes between ignorance and knowledge in cases of marriage during 'iddah, linking the severity of the penalty to the nature of the preceding divorce. For a revocable divorce (raj'ah), where the husband retains the right to remarry, the penalty is stoning (rajm), reflecting the higher sanctity of the marital bond; for an irrevocable divorce (ghair raj'ah), the standard flogging (hadd al-zani) applies. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the legal status of the 'iddah period as a continuation of the marital contract in specific contexts.
